title: Contextual permission lattice: RBAC v2 role model and enforcement constraints
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Design RBAC v2 role model that supports contextual permissions across resource hierarchies (organization -> workspace -> dedicated-pool -> model) and integrates with audit logging, SSO/SAML provisioning, and admin controls. Deliver a permissions lattice that enables: scoped delegations, time-bound elevated access, immutable audit trails for admin actions, and clear enforcement semantics for fallback policies (hosted -> dedicated -> private). This ticket covers the canonical data model, evaluation order, conflict resolution, enforcement hooks, and migration guidance from RBAC v1. Not in scope: UI polish for Console role editor (separate ticket), SAML IdP attribute mapping implementation (integration ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical role model (roles, permissions, resource-scope types) documented with examples for 5 common flows: tenant admin, workspace developer, service account, auditor, delegated support
Permission evaluation algorithm specified (pseudocode) showing precedence, inheritance, explicit deny handling, and caching invalidation points
Audit log schema entries defined for role assignment changes, inheritance changes, admin overrides, and transient elevation events
SSO/SAML provisioning mapping spec that supports group-to-role mapping and attribute-based scope constraints
Migration plan that maps RBAC v1 primary constructs to v2 equivalents and lists backward-incompatible behaviors and mitigation steps
decisions: Model: Use a first-class 'Scope' object with typed scope kinds (ORG, WORKSPACE, POOL, MODEL) rather than ad-hoc path strings to simplify policy evaluation and indexing
Evaluation order: nearest-scope explicit deny -> nearest-scope explicit allow -> inherited deny -> inherited allow -> default-deny; document deterministic tie-breakers for multiple allow rules
Delegation: Support role templates + binding objects; allow binding metadata like expires_at and delegate_reason to enable timebound elevation and auditability
Caching: Cache permission grants at (principal, scope, permission) with a short TTL and event-driven invalidation on role/binding changes
Migration: When migrating, create 'compat-role' bindings that emulate RBAC v1 implicit grants for 90 days and emit audit warnings to customers

comments: 2025-02-10 Ava Chen: Kickoff — captured scope kinds and high-level goals. Initial modeling session scheduled for 2025-02-12.

2025-02-12 Marco Rivera: Design session notes — agreed on typed Scope object; flagged complexity around model-level permission cardinality when model count scales (100k+). Recommended indexing strategy and partitioning by org_id.

2025-02-14 Priya Singh: Prototyped evaluation pseudocode. Observed worst-case O(N) with respect to bound roles per principal; recommend explicit per-principal materialized grants for hot principals (service accounts).
2025-02-16 Omar Patel: Audit schema proposal posted. Need decision on whether elevation reason is free text or enum; compliance prefers enum+free_text optional for proofs of intent.

2025-02-19 Lina Gomez: SSO mapping draft — SAML Group attributes will map to bindings; added proposal to support conditional role bindings based on SAML attributes (e.g., department=security => limited org-admin scope)
2025-02-20 Natalia Fong: Security review requested. Raised concern about timebound elevations being revocable before expiry and suggested immediate revocation semantics for emergency scenarios.
review_feedback: PM Review (E. Johnson): Ensure migration includes a grace period and telemetry to detect behavioral regressions
Design Review (S. Park): Prefer explicit deny semantics to be surfaced in Console logs to aid debugging
Compliance (N. Fong): Require retention policy for audit events of role changes to be at least 1 year by default for enterprise tenants
notes: Trade-offs considered: a fully policy-language approach (e.g., CEL) was rejected for initial rollout due to complexity and debugging overhead; chose typed roles+bindings for predictable enforcement and faster ramp. Plan to iterate to more expressive policies in v2.1 once we have stable telemetry.
migration_notes: Create compat bindings script that scans RBAC v1 grants, emits mapping suggestions, and offers an opt-in dry-run. Communicate breaking changes in permission inheritance to customers with examples and CLI tools. Provide admin console report listing users who gain/lose permissions post-migration.
qa_plan: Unit tests for evaluation algorithm covering inherit/deny/allow precedence
Integration tests across org->workspace->pool->model resource chains
Property-based tests for caching correctness and invalidation windows
Smoke tests for SAML provisioning and role-binding creation via IdP push
